title: Signature Proof Freshness Stamps
description: Signature edition: every cached proof carries a freshness stamp — prover version, dependency versions, and the date. Stale stamps (prover upgraded, dependency changed) are visibly marked and re-verified before use. A cached proof is trusted exactly as far as its stamp is fresh. This is a Signature original method.
method: Stamp caches with (prover, deps, date); mark stale on any change; re-verify before use; the stamp is part of the cache key.
usage: Never use a stale-stamped proof for release decisions; re-verify first.

demo.code:
print('cached proof: stamp (lean-4.7, mathlib-2024-01)')
print('prover now 4.8 -> STALE, re-verified before use')

title: Signature Lemma library reuse
description: Signature edition: Proved lemmas are the ultimate cache: a lemma proved once is reused in every future proof that needs it. Curated lemma libraries (mathlib in Lean, with 100k+ theorems) mean most proofs assemble existing results instead of proving from scratch — the community's shared proof cache.
method: Prove general lemmas; name and index them; future proofs cite lemmas; the library grows monotonically.
usage: Generalize lemmas before adding (specific lemmas rarely reuse); index by conclusion shape.

demo.code:
print('lemma add_comm proved once (2024)')
print('reused in 1,204 proofs since -> never re-proved')

title: Signature Counterexample cache for failed goals
description: Signature edition: Failed proof attempts are cached too: the goal plus its counterexample. When the same goal recurs, the cached counterexample immediately shows why it fails — no wasted solver time re-discovering unprovability, and the failure reason is documented.
method: Cache (goal -> counterexample) on failure; on recurrence, present the cached counterexample; clear when definitions change.
usage: Review cached failures periodically — a definition change may have fixed the goal.

demo.code:
print('goal G failed before: counterexample x=0 cached')
print('G recurs -> immediate: still fails, x=0 (no solver time wasted)')

title: Signature Distributed proof checking
description: Signature edition: Proof checking parallelizes beautifully: independent theorems check on separate machines. Cloud CI fans out thousands of theorems across workers, each verifying its share against the shared lemma database — full library verification in minutes, not hours.
method: Partition theorems by dependency levels; workers check their partition; a coordinator assembles the verified DAG.
usage: Partition by dependency level (level N needs level N-1 verified); cache aggressively between runs.

demo.code:
print('mathlib: 100k theorems / 64 workers -> full check 11min')
print('(single machine: 9 hours)')

title: Signature Proof repair across versions
description: Signature edition: Library upgrades break proofs; proof repair replays cached proofs against the new library, and where they fail, searches for small patches (renamed lemmas, reordered tactics) automatically. Cached proofs become the raw material for migration, not casualties of it.
method: Replay proofs on the new version; on failure, search local patches (lemma renames, tactic fixes); keep what patches cleanly, flag the rest.
usage: Run repair as part of every upgrade; review flagged proofs promptly.

demo.code:
print('upgrade lean 4.7 -> 4.8: 2,400 proofs replayed')
print('2,310 clean, 82 auto-patched, 8 flagged for humans')

title: Signature Cross-project proof sharing
description: Signature edition: Proofs are portable across projects using the same foundations: a verified sorting routine proved in one project is imported (not re-proved) by the next. Package managers for proofs (opam for Coq, reservoir for Lean) turn verification into shared infrastructure.
method: Publish verified components as packages; dependents import the proofs; version the proof packages like code.
usage: Publish general verified components; depend on proof packages instead of re-verifying.

demo.code:
print('import verified_sort (proof included)')
print('project uses it: 0 proof obligations (proof shipped with package)')

title: Signature Proof term sharing (hash-consing)
description: Signature edition: Proof terms share massive substructure; hash-consing stores each unique subterm once, with sharing by pointer. Developments that would use gigabytes as trees fit in memory as DAGs — the same trick Lisp and compilers use, applied to proofs.
method: Hash-cons all proof terms; equal subterms share storage; the proof is a DAG, not a tree.
usage: Enable hash-consing in the kernel; it's pure win (no soundness impact).

demo.code:
print('proof term: 2.1GB as tree -> 84MB as DAG (hash-consed)')
print('sharing: 96% of subterms shared')

title: Signature Incremental proof checking
description: Signature edition: When one definition changes, only proofs depending on it need re-checking. Incremental checkers track the dependency graph and re-verify the affected cone — Lean 4 and Coq's async checking turn full re-verification from minutes into seconds on typical edits.
method: Track proof dependencies; on change, re-check the dependent cone only; cache everything outside the cone.
usage: Keep the dependency graph fine-grained; the smaller the cone, the faster the re-check.

demo.code:
print('edit: def add (1 of 2,400 defs)')
print('dependent cone: 37 proofs -> re-checked in 4s (full: 38min)')

title: Signature Tactic result caching
description: Signature edition: Tactics like 'simp' do expensive work (rewriting with hundreds of lemmas) that repeats across goals. Caching tactic results keyed by (tactic, goal shape) skips the search on repeats — the automation gets faster the more it's used.
method: Key by (tactic name + args, normalized goal); cache the resulting proof term or failure; invalidate on lemma-set changes.
usage: Cache at the tactic level for expensive tactics; watch memory on huge developments.

demo.code:
print('simp on goal shape S: cached result reused')
print('1,204 simp calls -> 312 unique -> 74% cache hit rate')
